Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the RetailWave Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to RetailWave's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Thompson, CEO; Maria Lopez, CFO; David Chen, COO; and Lisa Patel, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, CEO of RetailWave.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust growth in our seller services and value-added services, alongside impressive seller performance metrics like our expanding active seller base and rising revenue per seller. We saw significant growth in key metrics, including GMV up 24% year-over-year to $79 billion and active sellers reaching 1.52 million.

Our focus remains on enhancing take rates through pricing optimizations and controlled promotions, while driving efficiency in operating expenses. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our Seller AI Copilot and WaveAds platform, which we believe will significantly boost ARPU and ecosystem lock-in.

We are investing heavily in fulfillment automation and AI-driven tools to support our marketplace scalability.

Finally, we are committed to delivering superior ROAS through channel optimizations and privacy-first strategies.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Lopez, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Maria Lopez:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $2.66 billion, an increase of 22% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42%, driven by higher adoption of high-margin value-added services and take rate expansion. Operating expenses were $1.82 billion, representing 68.4% of revenue, reflecting ongoing efficiency gains across fulfillment, marketing, and tech. On marketing spend, we achieved a blended ROAS of 5.6x, up 17% year-over-year, allowing us to drive incremental GMV with disciplined allocation.

Let me now dive deeper into these areas, starting with our Seller Services and Value-Added Services segment, which continues to be a high-margin growth engine for RetailWave. This powers our marketplace ecosystem, similar to Amazon's Seller Central or Shopify's merchant tools, but tailored for cross-border scalability among mid-market brands. In Q3 FY2024, this segment generated $482 million in revenue, up 38% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter, surpassing our overall revenue growth. It now represents 28% of total net revenue, up from 23% last year, highlighting its role in diversifying beyond traditional marketplace take rates on GMV.

Breaking it down, our active seller base expanded to 1.2 million, with 68% adopting at least one value-added service—a record, up from 52% in Q3 FY2023. This is driven by our Seller Pro Suite, bundling advertising, fulfillment, payments, and analytics into tiered plans that lift ARPU by 45% for Pro subscribers compared to basic listings. In advertising, we hit $215 million, up 42% year-over-year or 45% of the segment, with 41% seller adoption—up from 32%. Our AI-optimized WaveAds platform powers Sponsored Products and Display Ads, akin to Amazon DSP, improving click-through rates 27% via real-time bidding on 15 billion monthly shopper impressions, with take rates at 18% on ad spend. Video ads, drawing from TikTok Shop, added $28 million as our fastest-growing format.

Fulfillment and logistics via our RetailWave Fulfillment Network, or RFN, brought in $142 million, up 35% year-over-year and 29% of segment revenue. Adoption rose to 37% among eligible sellers, from 28%, with North America at 45% versus 22% in APAC after adding 150 new centers. RFN handles 18% of platform GMV, or $14.2 billion in Q3, offering 2-day Prime-like shipping to 85% of orders. Margins expanded 250 basis points to 32% through robotic picking from partners like Symbotic, mitigating Red Sea disruptions.

Payments and financial services contributed $89 million, up 32%, on $22 billion total payment volume, up 40%. Adoption is highest at 55%, with RetailWave Pay providing instant settlements and BNPL like Affirm or Klarna, at 2.8% take rates boosted by AI fraud detection cutting chargebacks 19%. Gross margins here are 62%. Other VAS like analytics and branding tools added $36 million, up 29%, with 22% adoption; our Insight360 dashboard uses generative AI for predictive inventory, yielding 15% GMV uplift for users.

Regionally, North America drove 62% of segment revenue with 72% adoption, aided by Shopify Plus integrations and 1.5% fulfillment fees. EMEA grew 45% to $112 million at 61% adoption, navigating GDPR with localized data centers and Euro BNPL. APAC surged 55% to $98 million, though at 49% adoption due to logistics fragmentation—partnerships with Lazada and Shopee aim for 60% by FY2025. LATAM added $45 million, up 62%, with Brazil's Pix boosting payments to 48%.

We've committed $250 million in FY2024 CapEx to VAS tech, including beta rollout of Seller AI Copilot to 50,000 sellers for automated listing and pricing, delivering 22% ARPU lift. Amid Temu/Shein price wars, sellers lean on VAS for differentiation, pushing segment take rate on GMV to 4.2% from 3.5%. Adoption rose 5-7 points quarter-over-quarter despite softening demand, with VAS users growing GMV 2.3x faster.

This segment's 55% adjusted EBITDA margins—versus 28% platform-wide—lifted operating margins 320 basis points year-over-year. VAS sellers show 3.2x lifetime value and 40% lower churn. We're targeting 75% adoption by FY2026 via freemium trials and Global Seller Academy. Amid 4.1% U.S. retail inflation and China tariffs, VAS drove 65% of incremental revenue. For Q4, we guide $510-530 million, up 32-37%, trending to 70% adoption in a $6.5 trillion e-commerce market where VAS grows 2x faster than GMV per McKinsey.

Shifting to seller performance metrics, which highlight our marketplace's scalability. We ended Q3 with 1.52 million active sellers—those generating at least $1,000 GMV over trailing 12 months—up 28% year-over-year from 1.19 million, outpacing Shopify's 20% and Amazon's mid-teens growth. Quarter-over-quarter, we netted 112,000, with 185,000 gross onboardings—a record. Churn is low at 4.2% annualized, down 80 basis points, via Seller Success Hub's ML recommendations cutting new-seller attrition 22%.

Seller ARPU hit $4,820, up 18% year-over-year from $4,090 and 5% sequentially, covering fees, fulfillment, ads, and tools like RFN. GMV per seller rose 9% to $128,000 trailing 12 months via Dynamic Pricing Engine boosting conversions 14% in electronics and fashion. Blended take rate expanded 110 basis points to 12.8%, from VAS adoption; RFN penetration is 62%, up from 48%.

Recent Q1'24 cohort tracks at $3,200 ARPU in first three months, 35% ahead, thanks to API integrations with SAP and QuickBooks slashing setup to under 2 hours. North America has 612,000 sellers at $6,100 ARPU in health & beauty. APAC reached 512,000, up 42%, at $2,900 ARPU growing 25%, with $450 million in Seller Financing loans. EMEA at 278,000, growth 18% despite DSA/Brexit, ARPU $4,200 via EU VAT tools. LATAM 118,000, up 32%, gaining on Mercado Libre in groceries.

We're prioritizing quality with Platinum tier for top 10% generating 45% revenue. GraphQL API v2.0 speeds uploads 30%, ML fraud cuts chargebacks to 0.8%. We expect 1.7 million sellers by year-end, mid-teens ARPU growth.

On operating expenses, we've achieved a 12% year-over-year reduction as a percentage of net revenue to 68.4% from 77.9%, ahead of Shopify and Wayfair. Total OpEx was $1.82 billion, up 8% nominally but flat to GMV at 24.5%, despite logistics inflation, apparel demand softness, and Temu pricing.

Fulfillment (42% of OpEx, $765 million) costs per unit fell 18% to $4.72 via 450 new AMRs boosting throughput 32%, labor down to 22%. ROI 3.2x. Shifted 25% APAC to 3PL like SF Express, cutting last-mile 14%; U.S. micro-hubs save $0.45/order. ReturnGuard AI cut returns costs 22% to $1.10.

Marketing (28%, $510 million) grew 5% despite 20% GMV rise, CAC $28 down 15%. AI personalization on Vertex AI hit 4.8x ROAS; loyalty via Prime (28 million members) cut retention $12/user, LTV:CAC 3.7:1.

Tech/content (15%, $273 million) down 2% to revenue via 85% AWS utilization, saving $18 million. Edge computing cut latency 40ms, conversions up 7%; AutoOptimize GPT-4o handles 2.5 million descriptions, organic traffic +15%.

G&A/customer service (15%, $273 million) flat via zero-based budgeting, 10% headcount trim to 42,000. AI chatbots handle 68% queries, costs $2.15 down 21%.

North America OpEx 65% of revenue; EMEA improved 10%; APAC 14% gains; LATAM leverage from fintech. Targeting mid-teens leverage H2, with 14.2% EBITDA margins up 320 bps.

Turning to advertising and marketing efficiency, our ROAS was 5.6x, up 17% from 4.8x, driving $2.8 billion revenue on $450 million budget, 35% of $8.1 billion GMV. Core ROAS 6.1x amid rising CPMs.

Search (35% spend) 8.2x via Performance Max, 28% incrementality. Social/video (40%) 4.9x, TikTok 7.4x. Display/DSP (20%) 3.8x, CTV 5.2x. Emerging 6.3x.

North America 6.4x; Europe 4.7x with CDP; APAC 7.2x. AI bidding cuts CPA 18%; MTA and geo-tests reallocate 25%. First-party data restores 20% iOS revenue. Targeting 6.5x, spend to 5.5% GMV.

Finally, take rate expanded to 18.5%, up 120 bps from 17.3%, driving marketplace revenue to $1.8 billion on $9.7 billion GMV, above Etsy/Wayfair averages.

Core marketplace 14.2%, ads +4.1 points. Electronics 16.8%, fashion 11.5%; ASP +8% to $45. Tiered fees for enterprises up 90 bps. Promos diluted 40 bps at 28% GMV, controlled by Merlin AI. NexBoost lifted ads 50 bps; ERP integrations shift to B2B.

North America 19.2%; Europe 17.8%; APAC 16.5%; LATAM 13.2% improved by fraud AI. Guide FY 18.7-19.1%, with ad acceleration.

Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended with $4.2 billion in cash and equivalents. We are reaffirming full-year guidance of $11-11.5 billion revenue, 14-16% EBITDA margins.

Now I'll turn it over to David to discuss operations.

David Chen:
Thanks, Maria. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and last-mile optimization. Our shipping times improved by 25% to average 1.8 days. Fulfillment costs declined 15% per unit through RFN expansions and AMR deployments. We are implementing edge computing and robotic systems across 200 centers globally, enhancing throughput amid regional disruptions.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa.

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, David. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from AI-personalized campaigns on Meta and TikTok Shop, alongside retail media expansions. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down 15%. Our brand awareness increased by 22% per Nielsen data. We are focusing on privacy-compliant first-party data and CTV for holiday ramps.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [pause] Our first question comes from Mike Rivera with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Rivera:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Maria, can you expand on the seller services adoption trends and how VAS is impacting margins amid macro headwinds?

Maria Lopez:
Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, as I detailed, VAS adoption hit 68% with standout growth in advertising at 41% and RFN at 37%. It's resilient, contributing 65% of incremental revenue despite inflation and tariffs, with 55% EBITDA margins juicing overalls by 320 bps. VAS users grow GMV 2.3x faster, locking in 3.2x LTV.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. On take rate, what drove the 120 bps expansion, and how sustainable with promo ramps?

Alex Thompson:
Emily, Maria covered the drivers well—pricing tiers added 90 bps, offset promo dilution via AI caps. Ads and mix shifts to electronics at 16.8% help. With moderating promos to 25% GMV, we see continued 100+ bps FY expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. David, on seller metrics, how are you ensuring quality with 28% growth, and APAC ARPU outlook?

David Chen:
Raj, quality via Platinum tiers—top 10% do 45% revenue. Churn at 4.2% thanks to Success Hub. APAC ARPU up 25% to $2,900, targeting 2.5x LTV via financing; partnerships accelerate to 60% VAS.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays.

Laura Kim:
Hi, thanks. Lisa, ROAS details—how are you navigating privacy changes for 6.5x target?

Lisa Patel:
Laura, strong question. First-party CDP captures 65%, LiveRamp resolves identity for 20% iOS lift. Channel shifts to TikTok 7.4x and CTV 5.2x, AI bidding cuts CPA 18%. Blended to 6.5x feasible, dipping spend to 5.5% GMV.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Thompson for closing remarks.

Alex Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders—leveraging VAS, seller growth, OpEx discipline, ROAS efficiency, and take rate expansion in this dynamic e-commerce landscape. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
